translations.text: Peter, the apostle of Jesus Christ, writes to the chosen people living in the Diaspora and in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.

According to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through the purification of the Spirit, for obedience in faith and sprinkling with the blood of Jesus Christ: may grace and peace be yours in abundance.
Blessed is God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who in his abundant mercy has given us birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
into an inheritance that cannot perish or be defiled and never fades, kept for you in heaven,
you who are protected by the power of God through faith for the salvation that is ready to be revealed at the last time.
You rejoice in this, though now, for a little while, if necessary, you have been grieved by various trials,
so that the proven worth of your faith, more precious than gold that perishes even though it is tested by fire, may be found to bring you praise, glory, and honor when Jesus Christ is revealed.
You love him though you have not seen him. And even now, though you do not see him, you believe in him and rejoice with a joy that is hidden and glorious,
as you receive the fulfillment of faith, the salvation of your souls.
The prophets searched and investigated this salvation, those who prophesied about the grace coming to you.
They sought to learn what time the Spirit of Christ within them was speaking about when he testified beforehand to the sufferings that would happen to Christ and the glories that would follow them.

It was revealed to them that they were serving not themselves but you in these things, which have now been announced to you through those who preached to you through the Holy Spirit sent from heaven—things that angels long to see.
Therefore, prepare your minds for action, remain sober, and place your hope fully in the grace that will be brought to you when Jesus Christ is revealed.
As obedient children, do not conform yourselves to your former desires, which you had in your ignorance.
Instead, just as the one who called you is holy, you yourselves must also be holy in all your conduct,
for it is written, “Be holy, because I am holy.”
And if you call the one who judges each person impartially according to their deeds “our Father,” live in fear during the time you are here,
knowing that you were not ransomed with perishable gold or silver from the empty practices your ancestors handed down to you,
but with the precious blood of Christ, the holy and undefiled lamb.
He was foreknown before the foundation of the world, but was revealed for your sake at the end of these times,
you who believe in God through his Son. God raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope would be in God.
Having purified your souls through obedience to the truth for brotherly love without hypocrisy, love one another with a holy heart.
You have been born not through a birth that perishes, but through one that cannot perish, through the living and enduring word of God.
For all flesh is like grass, and all its glory is like the flower of the grass. The grass has dried up, and its flower has fallen off,
but the word of the Lord remains forever. This is the word that was preached to you.
Therefore, put aside all malice, all deceit, all hypocrisy, all envy, and all slander.
Like little children who have just been born, desire the holy spiritual milk that contains no deceit, so that through it you may grow toward salvation.
If you have tasted that the Lord is good.
You are approaching him, the living stone, who was indeed rejected by people but is chosen and honored in God's sight.
You too are being built, like a living stone, into a spiritual house for holy service, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
For it is written in Scripture: “Look, I will place in Zion a chosen, honored cornerstone, and whoever believes in him will not be put to shame.”
The honor, then, belongs to you who believe. But for those who do not believe, “The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.”
And a stone that causes stumbling and a rock that causes offense for those who stumble at the word because they do not believe. They were appointed to this.
But you are a chosen race, a kingdom, a priesthood, a holy nation, a people destined for life, so that you may proclaim the wonders of the one who called you out of darkness into his wonderful light.
You who [?] a people at that time, but now are God's people; you who had not been shown mercy, but now have been shown mercy.
My beloved, I urge you, as strangers and foreigners, to keep away from bodily desires, which fight against the soul.
Maintain good conduct among the nations, so that, even where they speak against you as evildoers, they may see your good deeds and glorify God on the day of his visitation.
Submit yourselves to every human institution for the Lord's sake, whether to a king as the supreme authority,
or to governors as those sent by him to punish those who do evil and to honor those who do good.
For this is God's will: that by doing good you silence the ignorance of foolish people.
Live as free people, not having your freedom as a covering for wickedness, but as God's slaves.
Honor everyone. Love one another. Fear God. Honor the king.
Slaves, obey your masters with all reverence—not only those who are good and gentle, but also the harsh ones.
For it is commendable if someone, out of awareness of God, bears sorrows while suffering unjustly.
For what credit is there for you if you sin and endure being beaten? But if you do good and endure being beaten, this is commendable in God's sight.
For you were called to this, because Christ himself suffered for you, leaving you an example so that you might follow in his footsteps.
He committed no sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth.
When he was cursed, he did not curse in return. When he suffered, he did not threaten, but left it to the one who judges justly.
He carried our sins in his body onto the tree, so that, having died to sin, we might live in righteousness. By his wound you were healed.
For you were like sheep going astray, but now you have turned back to the shepherd, the overseer of your souls.
Likewise, wives should submit themselves to their husbands, so that even if some disobey the word, they may be won over without a word through their wives' conduct,
when they see your holy conduct in reverence.
But let their adornment not be outward adornment with braided hair, gold, and clothing,
but the hidden person of the heart, with the imperishable quality of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is precious in God's sight.
For this is how the holy women who hoped in God adorned themselves in former times, obeying their husbands,
as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him “my lord.” You have become her daughters if you do what is good and are not afraid of anything frightening.

Likewise, husbands, live with them with understanding, giving honor to your wives as the weaker vessel, because they are fellow heirs of the grace of life, so that you are not hindered in your prayers.
Finally, all of you should be united in heart, share one another's suffering, love one another as brothers and sisters, be compassionate, and humble yourselves.
Do not repay evil with evil or a curse with a curse. Instead, give a blessing, because you were called to this so that you might inherit a blessing.
For whoever wants to love life and see good days must restrain his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deceit.
Let him turn away from evil and do what is good. Let him seek; let him seek peace and pursue it.
For the Lord's eyes watch over the righteous, and his ears incline toward their plea, but the Lord's face is against those who do evil.
And who will harm you if you are eager to do what is good?
But even if you suffer for righteousness, you are blessed. Do not fear what they make you fear, and do not be troubled.
But honor Christ the Lord as holy in your hearts, always being ready to give a defense to anyone who asks you for an explanation of the hope within you,
but with gentleness and reverence, keeping a good conscience, so that those who insult your good conduct in Christ may be ashamed of the things they say against you.
For it is better to suffer while doing good, if that is God's will, than while doing evil.
For Christ died once for our sins, the righteous one for the unjust, to bring you near to God. He died in the flesh but lived in the spirit.
In this he went and preached to the spirits in prison,
who were disobedient in former times, when God waited patiently in the days of Noah while the ark was being built. A few fled into it and were saved through the water, eight souls in all.
This corresponds to baptism, which now saves you—not by washing dirt from the flesh, but by the response of a good conscience toward God, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
who is at God's right hand, having gone up into heaven, with angels, authorities, and powers made subject to him.
Christ, then, suffered in the flesh [?]. You too, arm yourselves with this thought: the one who died in the flesh has ceased from sin.
So that he may no longer live according to human desires, but spend the remaining days of his life according to God's will.
For the time that has passed is enough for you to have done what the Gentiles desire, living in impurity, lust, drunkenness, revelry, drinking bouts, and filthy idol worship.
They are astonished that you do not rush along with them into acts of excess, and they speak abusively.
They will give an account to the one who is ready to judge the living and the dead.
For this reason the good news was also preached to the dead, so that they might be judged according to human standards in the flesh, but live according to God in the spirit.
But the end of everyone has drawn near. Therefore, be clear-minded and sober for prayer.
Above all, maintain unfailing love for one another, because love covers a multitude of sins.
Be hospitable to one another without grumbling.
Use the gift each of you has received to serve one another, as good stewards of God's grace in its various forms.

Whoever speaks should speak as though his words are God's words. Whoever serves should serve with the strength God supplies, so that God may be glorified in everything through Jesus Christ, to whom belong glory and dominion forever. Amen.
My dear friends, do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal among you that is happening to test you, as though something strange were happening to you.
Instead, rejoice to the extent that you share in Christ's sufferings, so that you may also rejoice with great joy when his glory is revealed.
If you are insulted because of Christ's name, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and the power of God rests upon you. On their part, he is blasphemed, but on your part, he is glorified.
For none of you should suffer as a murderer, a thief, an evildoer, or someone who desires what does not belong to him.
But if someone suffers as a Christian, he should not be ashamed, but should glorify God because of this name.
For the time has come for judgment to begin with God's household. But if it begins with us first, what will be the end of those who disobey God's good news?
And if the righteous person is saved only with difficulty, where will the ungodly person and the sinner appear?
Therefore, let the others who suffer according to God's will entrust their souls to the faithful Creator while doing good.
Therefore, I urge the elders among you, as a fellow elder and a witness to Christ's sufferings, and as a steward of the glory that will be revealed:
Shepherd God's flock among you, not under compulsion, but willingly, in accordance with God; not out of greed for shameful gain, but eagerly.
Do not act as masters over those entrusted to you, but be examples to the flock,
so that when the chief Shepherd appears, you may receive the crown of glory that never fades.
Likewise, you younger people, obey the elders. And all of you, humble yourselves toward one another, because God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.
Therefore, humble yourselves under God's mighty hand, so that he may exalt you at the proper time.
Cast all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you.
Be sober and keep watch, because your adversary, the devil, walks about roaring like a lion, seeking to devour your souls.
Stand against him, firm in your faith, knowing that these same sufferings are being endured by your fellow believers throughout the world.

But the God of all grace, who called you into his eternal glory in Christ Jesus, will himself restore you after you have suffered a little while. He will make you firm, give you strength, and establish you on a foundation.
To him belong glory and dominion forever and ever. Amen.
Through Silvanus, whom I consider a faithful brother, I have written to you briefly, encouraging you and testifying that this is the true grace of God, in which you are to stand firm.
She who is chosen in Babylon greets you, as does Mark, my son.
Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace to all of you who are in Christ Jesus.
